threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: If you still call it Dalston Junction instead of just 'the Junction', you definitely haven't settled in yet.
Caught a bloke serenading the driver on the 59 last night, proper crooning. Made the journey to Streatham feel like a mini concert.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy in a full suit rummaging through a dumpster for a vintage record – only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find döner kebab shops open at 3 AM, serving fresh food to soothe late-night revelers right off the dance floor.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local would know that the smell of burnt toast lingers around Dolores Park when the fog rolls in. It hits different.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the 5-Fulton today, trying to pass the time. Just another day on Muni, where the unexpected is the norm.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Festa Major' is just a party, but it’s a month-long affair where locals bring their best carry dishes to share. It’s deep-rooted tradition.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell the newcomers by the way they take pictures of the metro maps. The locals just know where they’re going.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'bus stop' instead of 'the bus stop,' and your bag isn’t full of random takeaway menus from all the local spots.
Caught a late 333 and overheard a couple arguing about their takeaway order. Turns out he forgot the garlic bread—it's always the small things, innit?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy riding his bike home with a tree on his shoulder, like it was just a normal day. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a 24-hour Turkish döner shop where the same guy has been flipping meat since the early 90s, still remembers regulars by name.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they roll their eyes at the BART delays but still hit up the taqueria after a late night out, no matter what.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy dressed as a dinosaur calmly waiting for the bus at Turk and Leavenworth. Only in SF do we treat Muni delays like a costume party.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the tiny bars and local plazas where real life unfolds, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their unworn sneakers and the way they still pull out a map in the streets, looking lost.
